overview.label: The Complete Journey (Full Overview)
overview.description: Complete 49-node architecture map across all 6 design phases. Use Fit View [ ] or zoom into any cluster to inspect decisions and cross-phase trade-offs.

infraestructura_cluster.label: Infrastructure & Memory
infraestructura_cluster.description: Phase 0: Define the cluster manager and memory allocation strategy before running any code. This defines the operational limits.

contexto.label: Problem Context
contexto.description: Understand the business problem first. Data arrival rate, latency SLAs, and processing mode condition all subsequent Spark decisions.

datos.label: Data Characteristics
datos.description: Dataset size, distribution (skew), storage format, and governance (Catalogs & ACLs) determine physical execution strategies.

transformaciones.label: Transformation Types
transformaciones.description: Joins, GroupBys, and complex datatypes (Arrays, JSON) define the structural layout and shuffle cost of the pipeline.

ejecucion.label: Execution Implications
ejecucion.description: Analyze the DAG, shuffle impact, and task performance (speculative execution) to understand where the real bottlenecks are.

optimization.label: Optimization Strategies
optimization.description: Final tuning: partition management, caching, AQE runtime adaptation, and manual hints/tuning.

contexto.pregunta_guia: What does this pipeline need to solve and under what operational constraints?

modo_procesamiento.pregunta_guia: Do data arrive in discrete batches or as a continuous stream?

modo_streaming.pregunta_guia: What is the minimum acceptable latency: seconds (micro-batch) or milliseconds (continuous)?

slas_latencia.pregunta_guia: Are there defined SLAs? What is the maximum acceptable processing latency?

trade_latency_throughput.pregunta_guia: Do I optimize per-event response speed (latency) or total volume processed (throughput)?

datos.pregunta_guia: Which data properties shape the processing strategy?

tamano_datos.pregunta_guia: What is the order of magnitude? MB, GB, TB?

candidato_broadcast.nombre: Does the Dataset Fit in Memory for Broadcast?
candidato_broadcast.pregunta_guia: Does the small table fit within spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold (default 10MB)?

distribucion_datos.pregunta_guia: Are the data balanced across partitions or are there dominant keys?

data_skew.pregunta_guia: Are there significantly larger partitions? Are there keys with extreme cardinality?

formato_datos.pregunta_guia: Does the format support columnar read, efficient compression and partition pruning?

pushdown_lectura.pregunta_guia: Can filters and column selection be pushed down to the storage level before reading to memory?

transformaciones.pregunta_guia: Which transformation category dominates? Does it generate shuffle?

diseno_joins.pregunta_guia: Which physical join strategy minimizes shuffle given data size and distribution?

estrategia_fisica_join.nombre: Broadcast Hash vs Shuffle Hash vs Sort Merge Join
estrategia_fisica_join.pregunta_guia: BHJ if table is small. SHJ if data fits in memory. SMJ (default) if data is large and sortable.

agregaciones.pregunta_guia: Can the aggregation be fully pre-aggregated within each partition before shuffle?

hash_vs_sort_aggregate.pregunta_guia: Hash Aggregate is faster but requires the group to fit in memory. Sort Aggregate is spill-safe.

operaciones_ventana.pregunta_guia: Does the business logic require calculations over sorted data partitions (ranking, lag, rolling avg)?

particionado_ventana.pregunta_guia: Does the window partition key generate balanced distribution or amplify skew?

ejecucion.pregunta_guia: How are transformations materialized in the DAG stages? What bottlenecks do they generate?

impacto_shuffle.pregunta_guia: How many stage boundaries does the pipeline introduce? How much data moves across the network?

config_particiones_shuffle.pregunta_guia: Does the number of partitions yield ~100-200MB blocks? Is it too high (overhead) or too low (spill)?

analisis_dag.pregunta_guia: Does the DAG have redundant stages? Is an intermediate DataFrame reused multiple times?

recomputo_dataframe.nombre: Is the Same DataFrame Re-evaluated in Multiple Actions?
recomputo_dataframe.pregunta_guia: If a DataFrame triggers multiple action branches in the DAG without being persisted, it is fully recomputed each time.

optimization.pregunta_guia: Which techniques apply to reduce shuffle, avoid recomputation and manage memory efficiently?

control_particiones.pregunta_guia: Is there a need to redistribute data for load balancing or to reduce output files?

repartition_vs_coalesce.pregunta_guia: Repartition: generates shuffle, balances. Coalesce: no shuffle, only reduces without redistributing.

persistencia.pregunta_guia: Is it worth materializing this intermediate DataFrame to avoid costly recomputation?

cache_vs_checkpoint.pregunta_guia: Cache: fast, keeps lineage. Checkpoint: truncates the DAG lineage, writes to disk, more robust.

aqe.pregunta_guia: Is AQE enabled (Spark 3+)? What automatic optimizations does it offer for this pipeline?

capacidades_aqe.nombre: Dynamic Coalesce + Dynamic Join + Skew Join
capacidades_aqe.pregunta_guia: AQE can change the execution plan entirely at runtime: coalesces post-shuffle, converts to broadcast and splits skewed partitions.

infraestructura_cluster.pregunta_guia: Which resource manager will coordinate the executors and how is memory managed?

infra_yarn.pregunta_guia: Classic enterprise choice. Integrated with HDFS and MapReduce ecosystems.

infra_k8s.pregunta_guia: Modern cloud-native choice. Dockerized executors and isolation.

gestion_memoria.pregunta_guia: How will Spark allocate RAM between execution and storage caches?

manejo_estado.pregunta_guia: Do we need to aggregate data across multiple batches (e.g. rolling totals, sessionization)?

watermarking.pregunta_guia: How long should Spark wait for late-arriving data before clearing state?

modos_salida_streaming.pregunta_guia: How do we write the aggregated results? Append, Update, or Complete?

gobernanza_datos.pregunta_guia: How will users discover this dataset and who is allowed to access it?

sistema_catalogo.pregunta_guia: Should we register tables in a central metastore for SQL access and lineage tracking?

control_acceso.pregunta_guia: Do we need Fine-Grained Access Control (row/column level) or is storage-level IAM enough?

tipos_complejos.pregunta_guia: Are we working with nested structures (JSON, Maps, Arrays)?

manejo_arrays.pregunta_guia: Do we flatten arrays into rows (explode) or modify them inline (transform SQL HOF)?

extraccion_json.pregunta_guia: Should we extract single string fields or parse the whole JSON into a Spark Struct?

manejo_rezagados.pregunta_guia: Are some tasks randomly much slower due to hardware issues or bad nodes?

optimizacion_avanzada.pregunta_guia: Can we manually guide the Catalyst optimizer when statistics fail?

hints_sql.pregunta_guia: Should we force a Join strategy if the optimizer guesses the table size incorrectly?

max_partition_bytes.pregunta_guia: Are we reading millions of tiny files or huge non-splittable chunks?

edges.e01: The chosen processing mode defines the achievable latency range. Batch cannot guarantee sub-minute latencies.
edges.e02: Dataset size directly dictates if Broadcast Join applies. Above threshold, it is ruled out.
edges.e03: If dataset meets the broadcast threshold, BHJ is the optimal default choice.
edges.e04: An unbalanced key distribution produces unequally sized partitions, manifesting as Data Skew.
edges.e05: Data Skew acts severely upon Sort Merge Join: a single partition concentrates most workload.
edges.e06: With AQE enabled, the Skew Join optimizer splits overloaded partitions at runtime.
edges.e07: If a window partition key matches a skewed key, the corresponding executor will overload.
edges.e08: Any join other than BHJ introduces a stage boundary and a full shuffle operation.
edges.e09: groupBy/agg operations inherently generate shuffle to gather identical rows from different partitions.
edges.e10: Window functions trigger shuffle to partition and sort data.
edges.e11: Post-shuffle data volume dictates the optimal number of partitions to maintain ~128-200MB blocks.
edges.e12: AQE acts at shuffle materialization points, dynamically adjusting resulting partition count.
edges.e13: If an intermediate DF is the source for multiple actions, recomputation triggers the need to persist.
edges.e14: Columnar formats (Parquet, ORC) natively support projection pushdown. CSV/JSON do not.
edges.e15: Effective pushdown trims data volume read into memory, alleviating downstream size limits.
edges.e16: Excessive shuffle prompts the need for physical partition control (repartition/coalesce).
edges.e17: Strict SLAs may prohibit checkpoints (disk writes) due to the additional latency introduced.
edges.e18: Prioritizing throughput implies more partitions (parallelism). Latency requires fewer tasks.
